title: Capacity You Can Write, Directions You Can Read
summary: Follow product-key memory from billion-parameter capacity through 128B scaling and sparse slot updates, then contrast it with an SAE read-out that diagnoses and steers an existing model without enlarging that model.
learning_goals: Explain how sparse lookup makes a very large learned value table usable without activating all of its capacity.
Distinguish adding writable model parameters from fitting an auxiliary read-out over activations that already exist.
State sparse memory finetuning's low-interference result as this paper's measured claim, not as a guarantee of sparse updates.
